families.name: Information Availability & Exposure
families.definition: Whether behavior-relevant information is present, discoverable, noticeable, current, and encountered for sufficient time at a decision point.
families.includes: Include message availability, salience, recency, cues, and exposure duration.
families.exclusions: Exclude platform access and ranking, physical placement, and the recipient’s attention state.

families.name: Information Volume, Density & Load
families.definition: Objective amount, rate, density, and length of information presented within a defined exposure window.
families.includes: Include item count, arrival rate, message length, and content density.
families.exclusions: Exclude subjective overload and cognitive capacity, which are Psychological.
representativeDrivers: Information Volume Relative to Exposure Window

families.name: Clarity, Complexity & Completeness
families.definition: Linguistic and structural properties governing how explicit, readable, ambiguous, conflicting, or complete a message is.
families.includes: Include readability, complexity, ambiguity, completeness, contradiction, and uncertainty expression.
families.exclusions: Exclude comprehension, confusion, numeracy, and perceived uncertainty.

families.name: Framing & Presentation
families.definition: How substantively similar content is worded, ordered, formatted, or visually represented.
families.includes: Include gain/loss and attribute frames, probability formats, metaphors, ordering, and graphics.
families.exclusions: Exclude interface ranking and any claim that one frame is universally superior.

families.name: Argument & Evidence Quality
families.definition: Strength, amount, type, traceability, and explanatory structure of reasons and evidence supporting a claim.
families.includes: Include logical strength, evidence quality and amount, quantitative or exemplar evidence, citations, and causal explanation.
families.exclusions: Exclude recipient elaboration and institutional evidence rules.

families.name: Source Disclosure & Provenance
families.definition: Information conveyed about who produced a claim, their relevant qualifications and interests, and the claim’s origin and processing history.
families.includes: Include identity, credentials, track record, motive, conflicts, provenance, process transparency, and consensus cues.
families.exclusions: Exclude perceived credibility or trust and actual interpersonal relationships.

families.name: Repetition, Timing & Sequence
families.definition: Frequency, spacing, timing, ordering, and cross-source convergence of exposures.
families.includes: Include repetition, spacing, correction delay, sequence, and convergence across identifiable sources.
families.exclusions: Exclude algorithmic amplification and memory or familiarity states.

families.name: Narrative, Exemplification & Vividness
families.definition: Message features that organize information as stories, cases, concrete imagery, emotional content, or warnings.
families.includes: Include narrative form and coherence, exemplars, vividness, emotional valence/intensity, and warning content.
families.exclusions: Exclude narrative transportation, emotion experienced, and culturally shared master narratives.

families.name: Relevance, Tailoring & Audience Match
families.definition: Message adaptations that align content with a specified person, location, language, culture, or audience context.
families.includes: Include personalization, local specificity, linguistic accessibility, and cultural-context match.
families.exclusions: Exclude felt self-relevance, identity, and automated targeting systems.

families.name: Risk, Threat & Efficacy Content
families.definition: Stated information about severity, likelihood, susceptibility, response efficacy, and uncertainty of consequential outcomes.
families.includes: Include communicated threat, vulnerability, efficacy, and risk magnitude.
families.exclusions: Exclude fear, perceived threat, perceived vulnerability, and efficacy beliefs.

families.name: Feedback, Comparison & Norm Claims
families.definition: Communicated information about performance, progress, benchmarks, prevalence, approval, or consensus.
families.includes: Include performance feedback, comparative benchmarks, descriptive-norm claims, and consensus claims.
families.exclusions: Exclude actual norms, social approval, rank, and feedback-delivery technology.

families.name: Veracity, Omission & Correction
families.definition: Accuracy, misleadingness, omission, correction, retraction, and explanatory content that updates a claim.
families.includes: Include factual veracity, omission magnitude, correction presence/detail/specificity, and alternative explanations.
families.exclusions: Exclude belief accuracy and deliberate intent unless separately evidenced.

families.name: Action Guidance & Instructional Content
families.definition: Message features that specify a recommended action, implementation steps, timing, and decision-relevant constraints.
families.includes: Include recommendation specificity, calls to action, step completeness, and deadline specificity.
families.exclusions: Exclude behavior itself, opportunity, enforcement, and interface affordances.
